A conditional statement of test logic: if parity holds, the payment statistics will not differ. It asserts no expected outcome in either direction and no DOL action. The finder's reading that the data will show lower mental-health rates is tone, not words. The request that the DOL run the comparison is a proposal.
Promise of the next article in the author's own newsletter. Own content.
Promise of a follow-up article in the author's own newsletter. Own content.

'Is projected' passes on an unnamed external projection rather than the author's own expectation. The projection also names no year and no data series, so no quantity event could be written without inventing both.
'Anything that gets in the way of that spending going up ... can not be allowed' names no payer action, benchmark, countable set or date. No observable event can be written from the words.
Promise of part II of the author's own newsletter series. Own content.
Promise of further installments of the author's own newsletter series. Own content.

Present-tense estimate of average remission durability after accelerated TMS ('We understand ... it's between 12 and 18 months'). It states information about the current evidence, not a future state, and no third party decides it. As a science claim it also falls outside the five areas.
'May work for other indications' names no indication, trial, sponsor or regulatory decision. 'Other indications' is a quantifier with no countable set, and 'work' has no benchmark.

An evaluation ('a step backward for women, families, and medicine') and a rhetorical question. No future state is asserted in the words; the substitution of zuranolone for brexanolone is only implied by the finder's reading.
The author's own purchasing decision for his clinic. His organization decides.

Retrospective description of the photobiomodulation evidence base ('I have yet to see a paper'). The hedge 'this is not to say there could not be such a paper' concedes a possibility but asserts no expectation in either direction.
'It' is the national suicide trend in the CDC report, a population health outcome outside the five areas. The condition 'until we call a spade a spade' is also not observable.
Publishing schedule of the author's own newsletter. Own organization.

'If physicians prescribe this medical device ... they may avoid stimulants in many cases' names no countable set of prescribers or prescriptions, no series and no threshold. 'In many cases' is a quantifier without a countable set. The author's own practice (Fermata) prescribes the device.
Habitual present description of the ongoing stimulant shortage ('every stimulant prescription—these days—means'). No future state beyond the present is asserted.
'This is how we solve the ADHD treatment crisis—with better treatments!' is a slogan. No entity, adoption metric, benchmark or date can be written.
'We solve ADHD at scale' has no observable event, benchmark or countable set; 'things that aren't scalable' is undefined. Nothing can be written without inventing a metric.
'A hard limit on the amount of frustration anybody is going to put up with' implies prescribers will move away from stimulants, but names no countable set, series, threshold or date.
The author's own forthcoming paper. Own publication. 'I don't know how long that effect will be durable' asserts nothing.

A quip that the author's TwitterGPT profile 'will require a threads instance'. The literal claim concerns his own tool; the implied claim that Threads displaces or rivals Twitter/X has no benchmark, series or date. Nothing observable can be written.
Self-deprecating call about the author's own future audience. Audience attention for a newsletter is outside the five areas; 'niche status' and 'pay attention' also have no benchmark.
General claim about the quality of ChatGPT output. Not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice outcome; 'milquetoast and unsatisfying' has no benchmark.
General claim that language models trained on their own output degrade. Not one of the five areas; no benchmark or date.
General claim about the ceiling of generative AI ('regression to the mean'). Not one of the five areas; no benchmark or date.
Same sentence ('you will get a very brutal regression to the mean') in the same post as owen-0686, captured twice; the first row stands. The claim is in any case outside the five areas.
Statement about police killings, from a 2020 recording republished in 2023. Not one of the five areas.
Generalization about police behavior in mental health crises, from a 2020 recording. Not one of the five areas; 'more often than not' and 'about a thousand times a year' describe a present rate.

'We will solve a lot of arguments' has no observable event, countable set or benchmark; 'a lot of' is a quantifier without a set. The condition (the DOL adopting the author's p-value test) is his own proposal, and no adoption is forecast.
General claim about what large language models miss in training data. Not one of the five areas; no benchmark or date.
'A New Era' is a slogan, and 'it works. Reliably.' is a present-tense efficacy claim with no benchmark, adoption metric or date. Nothing observable can be written for SAINT from these words.
The author's own decision to drop medication management from his practice. His organization decides.
'Neuromodulation is the future of the field' is a slogan with no metric, benchmark, countable set or date.

'Never going to be something that got to market at scale' is a comparative with no threshold, series or benchmark for Zyprexa Relprevv sales or use; 'was always' frames it as retrospective. No quantity event can be written without inventing a threshold.

Incentive analysis in the present tense ('is not in their economic interest'). It explains why Sunovion has not funded mania research; it asserts no future action or inaction by Sunovion. The forecast is only implied.

Market-size figures to two decimals for 2023 and 2030 restate an unnamed market-research projection as background fact, not the author's own expectation. The words also name no data series, so a quantity event could not be written without inventing one.

event.entity: Magnus Medical (supplier) and adopting US hospitals
event.title: SAINT becomes available to patients in a US hospital setting
event.proposition: SAINT (fMRI-guided accelerated iTBS) is offered to patients in at least one US hospital setting, as announced by Magnus Medical or the hospital.
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of the definitive public announcement (Magnus Medical press release or the hospital's own public announcement) that SAINT is available to patients in a US hospital setting (inpatient or hospital outpatient department), or that a first patient has been treated with SAINT at a US hospital. Availability only through Magnus Medical's open-label dose-optimization study at non-hospital clinics, a hospital's stated intention or agreement to install without patient availability, and any CMS payment decision by itself do not count. Intake reading: 'available in hospital settings' = at least one US hospital offers SAINT to patients.

resolution_source.name: Magnus Medical press releases; the adopting hospital's public announcement

readings: 'available in hospital settings' = at least one US hospital offers SAINT to patients (inpatient or hospital outpatient department); one hospital suffices.

'under the new technology add-on payment program' is the payment route the forecaster names, not a separate forecast of a CMS decision; the item does not resolve on any CMS action, so the sentence is one event, not an 'A and B' split.

records.stage_note: At the statement date the forecaster describes SAINT as available outpatient only through Magnus Medical's open-label dose-optimization study, and names the NTAP program as the hospital payment route; no hospital availability is claimed yet. No class in base-rates.json covers first hospital availability of a cleared device, so b is null.
records.note: Admitted: hospitals and Magnus Medical, not the forecaster's organizations, decide whether SAINT is offered in a hospital; his company only helps hospitals obtain it, so this is not CONTROL. Flat future assertion ('and soon, in hospital settings') with no hedge is read as 'will', bin A, asserts true. 'Soon' is not a deadline: deadline null, undated panel with the 24-month window. affiliated true: in the same post the forecaster discloses that he started a company to help hospitals get SAINT, and his clinic Acacia is a trial site for the Magnus Medical study he names. The first clause (outpatient availability through the Magnus study) is a present fact, not a forecast.
